author: claude (chat) · weekly
summary: THREE THINGS MATTER THIS WEEK. (1) CRASH RADAR FLIPPED AMBER (26) for the first time — action is TIGHTEN: no new buys, obey tripwires, keep the full cash+gold sleeve. Drivers: SMH broke BELOW its 50d (still above 200d), HYG still under its 200d (red, credit stress), and book drawdown deepened to -18.7% (amber rung). Crucially still zero per-holding regime breaks — every name has 30d Sharpe z > -0.75 and trend > 45. (2) LEADERSHIP LEFT SEMIS. Cybersecurity now reigns BOTH horizons (mid 89 / long 90, +11.4% 1m) while Memory/HBM fell to 74/88 with 1m -11.6%. The book is 8 semis in a market that has rotated to cyber — that is the real reason for the drawdown, not a broken thesis. Every single one of the 8 holdings is now 'UPTREND with ADX FALLING' — uniform deceleration, no name broken. (3) July 20 rebalance: LRCX back IN, AMD OUT (AMD's 4th round-trip). Portfolio $1,218.17, +4.74% since May 9 inception, maxDD -18.7%, Sharpe 0.62. Equity curve whipsawed: $1,272 (Jul 13) → $1,131 (Jul 20) → $1,218 (Jul 25). CODE AUDIT: measured 634% annualized turnover in the live book (AMD in/out 4x in 10 weeks). Built and A/B tested three profitability enhancements (rank hysteresis, correlation-aware selection, radar-scaled exposure) over 2024-2026, 133 weekly rebalances, net of 10/25/50bps friction. ALL THREE LOST — baseline +566% beat hysteresis +441%, correlation +473%, radar +442%, all-three +343%, and won at every friction level. Shipped DISABLED with the results documented in code. Honest caveat: the test window contains no true bear market, so it is structurally biased against defensive measures.

RADAR.headline: AMBER 26 — first non-green reading. Tighten, don't panic.
RADAR.narrative: Crash radar: 26/100 AMBER. Red flag is credit (HYG below its 200d). Amber flags: SMH lost its 50d, book DD -18.7%. Green across VIX (16.9, term structure 0.87 steep contango), breadth 61%, yen calm, rates +9bp, curve +0.85%. Action per the ladder: NO new buys, obey tripwires strictly, keep the full 10% cash + 5% gold sleeve, re-check mid-week. This is not the ORANGE/RED de-risking zone — that starts at 40.

This is textbook late-stage deceleration inside intact structures.

If following mechanically, buy it; if you value the tripwire logic over the rank, AMD is the better hold and this swap is skippable.

But it currently has the BEST metrics of any candidate: trend 75, 30d Sharpe z +0.32, edge 66, 1m +3.8% (the only holding that is up on the month, vs -11% to -24% for the rest), 3m +77.8%. The mechanical rotation is churning a strong name out for a weaker one, and this exact pattern (AMD in/out 4x) is the churn the turnover audit flagged.

Memory/HBM, the book's core, fell to 74/88 with 1m -11.6%. This is the cleanest explanation for the drawdown: the book is concentrated in the theme money left, not in the theme money went to. If you want tactical exposure now, that is an off-strategy decision — NET remains the cleanest entry of the cyber complex.

LITE.headline: Full recovery from last week's WEAK: trend 48→68, only holding flat on the month.
LITE.narrative: Last week LITE was the book's WEAK tripwire (trend 48, 30d z -1.09σ, 1m -19.2%). One week later: trend 68, 30d z -0.14σ, 1m +0.7%, RSI 53. It reverted exactly as the mean-reversion argument predicted, which is why the discipline is to not sell at -2.4σ. Concrete evidence for holding oversold names inside intact regimes.

CODE_AUDIT.headline: 3 profitability enhancements built, A/B tested, ALL REJECTED — shipped disabled.
CODE_AUDIT.narrative: Measured 634% annualized turnover live (AMD 4 round-trips). Built rank hysteresis (buffer zone), correlation-aware greedy selection, and radar-scaled exposure; A/B tested over 2024-01-01..2026-07 (133 weekly rebalances) net of 10/25/50bps friction. Results — baseline +566% gross / DD -22.3% / Sharpe 2.17 / net@50bps $120,253 WINS. Hysteresis +441%, DD WORSE at -25.4%, cut turnover 761→422%/yr. Correlation +473%, DD better at -21.2% (only variant to improve DD). Radar exposure +442%, DD unchanged, vol 37→35. All three combined +343%. Baseline won at every friction level, so all three are shipped DISABLED behind flags with the results documented in backtest.ts. Interpretation: in a relentless momentum regime, fast rotation into the newest leader IS the alpha — damping it costs more than the friction saved. Caveat that matters: the window has no true bear market, so it is structurally biased against defensive measures. The correlation penalty is the most defensible and should be re-tested before the next real drawdown regime.
